QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_2

question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund (Cat III open-ended) has High-Water Mark NAV/unit of INR 1,250 and Reference Hurdle NAV/unit of INR 1,210 at year-end. Current NAV (pre-incentives) is INR 1,240/unit. Is the manager eligible for incentive fees?

answer.text: Yes, because NAV is above Reference Hurdle
Yes, because NAV is above the initial INR 1,000 subscription price
No, because NAV is below the High-Water Mark even though it is above Hurdle
Yes, incentive is calculated on (1,240 − 1,210) = INR 30/unit

explanation.text: The Logic: Minimum NAV eligible for incentive = higher of HWM (1,250) and Reference Hurdle (1,210) = INR 1,250/unit. Current NAV 1,240 is below 1,250 → NOT eligible. HWM acts as an extra threshold to prevent fees on losses already suffered by existing unit-holders. The Trap: Option A/D ignore HWM — classic trap. B is irrelevant (subscription price is only the Year-1 HWM). A manager who clears Hurdle but is still below HWM does NOT earn carry. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D Cat I/II Manager uses drawdown waterfalls with hurdle + catch-up; HWM is Cat III (open-ended, daily/monthly NAV) and is the primary mechanism tested on XIX-E. Manager's Pro-Tip: After a drawdown, HWM stays frozen till NAV reclaims the prior peak. Till then, incentive accrual is zero even on strong positive months — explain this clearly in the PPM to avoid investor disputes when the fund recovers.
